questions.question: Ashish has ₹1218 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Arun and Mahesh and asked them to invest it at 10% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Arun and Mahesh got same amount after 11 and 12 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Ashish give to Mahesh?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When amounts are equal at Compound Interest, the ratio of the principals is directly related to the multiplying factors based on the time difference.

Ratio of Arun's share to Mahesh's share = (1 + 10/100)¹²−¹¹ : 1 = 11 : 10

Total ratio parts = 11 + 10 = 21 parts

21 parts = ₹1218 ⇒ 1 part = ₹58

Mahesh's share = 10 parts = 10 × 58 = ₹580

**∴ The correct answer is ₹580.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount = ₹1218

Rate of interest (R) = 10% compounded annually

Time for Arun (T₁) = 11 years

Time for Mahesh (T₂) = 12 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

questions.question: The greatest number, which divides 1938 and 2337 to leave 0 and 3 respectively as remainders, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The required number is the HCF of (1938 − 0) and (2337 − 3), which means we need the HCF of 1938 and 2334.

Instead of prime factorization, check the divisibility of both numbers using the given options.

Both 1938 and 2334 are even numbers, and the sum of their digits (21 and 12) are both divisible by 3.

Thus, both numbers are divisible by 2 × 3 = 6.

Other options (11, 13, 14) do not completely divide 1938.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First number = 1938 with remainder 0

Second number = 2337 with remainder 3

**Formula Used:**

Required greatest number = HCF of (N₁ − R₁) and (N₂ − R₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ First exact divisible number = 1938 − 0 = 1938

⇒ Second exact divisible number = 2337 − 3 = 2334

⇒ We need to find the HCF of 1938 and 2334.

⇒ Prime factorization of 1938 = 2 × 3 × 17 × 19

⇒ Prime factorization of 2334 = 2 × 3 × 389

⇒ The common factors are 2 and 3.

⇒ HCF = 2 × 3 = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF of Remainders Case

To find the greatest number dividing x, y and z leaving remainders a, b and c respectively, calculate the HCF of (x−a), (y−b) and (z−c).

LCM with Same Remainder Case

To find the smallest number which when divided by x, y and z leaves remainder r in each case, calculate LCM(x, y, z) + r.

Product of Two Numbers

For any two natural numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: A × B = HCF(A, B) × LCM(A, B).
</p

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

Successive Percentage

questions.question: If the ratio of radius of the bases of two cylinders is 4 : 5 and the ratio of their heights is 5 : 2, then the ratio of their volumes is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume ratio = (Ratio of radii)² × (Ratio of heights)

V₁ : V₂ = (4 / 5)² × (5 / 2)

V₁ : V₂ = (16 / 25) × (5 / 2) = 8 : 5

**∴ The correct answer is 8 : 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of radius of the bases, r₁ : r₂ = 4 : 5

Ratio of their heights, h₁ : h₂ = 5 : 2

**Formula Used:**

Volume of a cylinder (V) = πr²h

**Calculations:**

⇒ Ratio of volumes = V₁ : V₂

⇒ V₁ : V₂ = (π × r₁² × h₁) : (π × r₂² × h₂)

⇒ V₁ : V₂ = (r₁ / r₂)² × (h₁ / h₂)

⇒ V₁ : V₂ = (4 / 5)² × (5 / 2)

⇒ V₁ : V₂ = (16 / 25) × (5 / 2)

Volume of a Cylinder

The volume of a right circular cylinder is calculated by multiplying the area of its base by its height using the formula: V = πr²h.

Curved Surface Area (CSA)

The area of the curved walls or lateral surface of a cylinder is given by the formula: CSA = 2πrh.

Total Surface Area (TSA)

The total surface area includes both the curved surface and the two circular flat bases, calculated as: TSA = 2πr(h + r).

questions.question: If at same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is ₹42 and compound interest is ₹49, then what is the principal (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

SI for 1st year = 42 ÷ 2 = ₹21

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = 49 − 42 = ₹7

Rate of interest (R) = (Difference ÷ SI for 1st year) × 100 = (7 ÷ 21) × 100 = 100/3%

Principal = (SI for 1st year × 100) ÷ R = (21 × 100) ÷ (100/3) = 21 × 3 = ₹63

**∴ The correct answer is ₹63.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

SI for 2 years = ₹42

CI for 2 years = ₹49

**Formula Used:**

Difference between CI and SI for 2 years = P(R/100)²

Simple Interest = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Simple Interest for 1 year = 42 ÷ 2 = ₹21

⇒ Difference (CI − SI) for 2 years = 49 − 42 = ₹7

Difference between CI and SI for 2 Years

The difference between compound interest and simple interest for a period of exactly two years is given by the formula: Diff = P(R/100)².

Difference between CI and SI for 3 Years

For a period of exactly three years, the difference formula extends to: Diff = P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).

Compound vs Simple Interest Mechanics

For the first year (when compounded annually), the Simple Interest and Compound Interest are always identical. From the second year onwards, Compound Interest generates an extra value which is simply the "Interest computed on the accumulated Interest" from the previous years.

questions.question: In a class, the average score of boys is 75 with 20 boys and the average score of girls is 85 with 30 girls. What is the overall average score of the class?

Ratio of Boys to Girls = 20 : 30 = 2 : 3

Assume the base average is 75 (boys' average).

Deviation of girls' average from base = 85 − 75 = +10

Rule of Alligation

Properties of Average

questions.question: Evaluate: 16 + 8 ÷ 4 - 3 × 4
questions.solution:
**Given:**

16 + 8 ÷ 4 - 3 × 4

**Formula Used:**

Order of operations: Parentheses → Exponents → Multiplication and Division (from left to right) → Addition and Subtraction (from left to right).

**Calculation:**

⇒ 16 + 8 ÷ 4 - 3 × 4

⇒ 16 + 2 - 12 (division and multiplication performed first)

⇒ 18 - 12 (addition performed next)

⇒ 6 (subtraction performed last)

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

questions.question: A and B can finish a piece of work in 15 days and 20 days, respectively. If A and B work on alternate days, how many days will it take to complete the work (A starts the work)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total Work = LCM(15, 20) = 60 units.

Efficiency of A = 4 units/day, Efficiency of B = 3 units/day.

Work done in 2 days (1 cycle of A and B) = 4 + 3 = 7 units.

In 16 days (8 cycles), work done = 8 × 7 = 56 units.

Remaining 4 units are completed by A on the 17th day exactly in 1 day.

**∴ The correct answer is 17 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by A = 15 days

Time taken by B = 20 days

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work done by A on day 1 = 4 units

⇒ Work done by B on day 2 = 3 units

⇒ Total work done in 2 days = 4 + 3 = 7 units

⇒ Multiply by 8 to reach closest to total work: Work done in 16 days = 7 × 8 = 56 units

⇒ Remaining work = 60 − 56 = 4 units

⇒ On the 17th day, it is A's turn to work.

⇒ Time taken by A to complete remaining 4 units = 4 ÷ 4 = 1 day

Alternate Day Work

In alternate day problems, identify the total work done in one complete cycle of days, calculate the maximum full cycles possible without exceeding total work, and then manually track the remaining work day by day.

Pipes & Cisterns

Similar to the Time & Work concept, filling pipes have positive efficiency while emptying pipes (leaks) have negative efficiency.

Work & Wages

Wages are strictly distributed in the ratio of the total work done by each individual. If they work for the same number of days, the wages can directly be distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.
</p

Fourth Proportion

If four numbers a, b, c, and d are in proportion (a : b :: c : d), then d is called the fourth proportional. It is calculated as d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Third Proportion

Mean Proportion

</p

questions.question: The largest four-digit number which when divided by 9, 18 and 23, leaves a remainder 5 in each case, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The required number must be of the form: LCM(9, 18, 23) × k + 5.

The LCM of 9, 18, and 23 is 414.

The largest 4-digit number is 9999. Dividing 9999 by 414 gives a quotient of 24 and a remainder of 63.

Largest 4-digit multiple of 414 = 9999 − 63 = 9936.

Required number = 9936 + 5 = 9941.

**∴ The correct answer is 9941.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Divisors: 9, 18, and 23

Remainder in each case = 5

**Formula Used:**

Required Number = [Largest 4-digit multiple of LCM of the divisors] + Remainder

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, find the prime factorization to calculate the LCM of 9, 18, and 23.

⇒ 9 = 3²

⇒ 18 = 2 × 3²

⇒ 23 = 23 (Prime number)

⇒ LCM = 2 × 3² × 23 = 18 × 23 = 414

⇒ The largest 4-digit number is 9999.

⇒ Divide 9999 by the LCM (414) to find the largest multiple within the 4-digit range.

⇒ 9999 ÷ 414 = 24 with a remainder of 63.

⇒ The largest 4-digit multiple of 414 = 9999 − 63 = 9936.

⇒ This implies that 9936 is completely divisible by 9, 18, and 23.

⇒ Since we need a remainder of 5 in each case, we add 5 to this multiple.

⇒ Required number = 9936 + 5 = 9941.

**∴ The correct answer is 9941.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM Method for Same Remainder

When a number is divided by a, b, and c leaving the same remainder r in each case, the general form of that number is LCM(a, b, c) × k + r.

LCM Method for Different Remainders

When a number divided by a, b, and c leaves remainders x, y, and z respectively, and the differences (a−x) = (b−y) = (c−z) = d are equal, the number is in the form LCM(a, b, c) × k − d.

HCF for Same Remainder

The greatest number that divides x, y, and z leaving the same remainder in each case is the HCF of |x−y|, |y−z|, and |z−x|.
</p

questions.question: A book was purchased for ₹1,020 and sold for ₹1,224. Find the profit percentage.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Selling Price to Cost Price = 1224 ÷ 1020 = 6 / 5

Profit parts = 6 − 5 = 1 part

Profit % = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ The correct answer is 20%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹1,020

Selling Price (SP) = ₹1,224

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage

When Selling Price is less than Cost Price, a loss occurs. Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount. Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

Successive Profit / Loss

If an item is sold multiple times, the final SP is calculated by applying successive percentage changes: Final SP = Initial CP × (1 + P₁/100) × (1 + P₂/100).

questions.question: The average weight of Mohammad, Ashish and Kiran is 46 kg. If the average weight of Mohammad and Ashish be 40 kg and that of Ashish and Kiran be 42 kg, then the weight of Ashish (in kg) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total sum of all three = 46 × 3 = 138 kg

Sum of Mohammad and Ashish = 40 × 2 = 80 kg

Sum of Ashish and Kiran = 42 × 2 = 84 kg

Weight of Ashish = (Sum of Mohammad & Ashish) + (Sum of Ashish & Kiran) − Total Sum

Weight of Ashish = 80 + 84 − 138 = 26 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 26 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 

 
 Mohammad + Ashish = 80 kg

 
 Ashish + Kiran = 84 kg

 
 Total (M + A + K) = 138 kg

 
• 
 
 
 Ashish overlap

**Given:**

Average weight of Mohammad, Ashish, and Kiran = 46 kg

Average weight of Mohammad and Ashish = 40 kg

Average weight of Ashish and Kiran = 42 kg

**Formula Used:**

Total Value = Average × Number of entities

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total weight of Mohammad, Ashish, and Kiran = 46 × 3 = 138 kg

⇒ Total weight of Mohammad and Ashish = 40 × 2 = 80 kg

⇒ Total weight of Ashish and Kiran = 42 × 2 = 84 kg

⇒ Weight of Ashish = (Total weight of M & A) + (Total weight of A & K) − (Total weight of M, A, & K)

⇒ Weight of Ashish = 80 + 84 − 138

⇒ Weight of Ashish = 164 − 138

⇒ Weight of Ashish = 26 kg

**∴ The correct answer is 26 kg.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Missing Observation in Average

If the average of N items is given, and the averages of the first 'a' and last 'b' items are given where a + b > N, the overlapping item = (Sum of first 'a' items + Sum of last 'b' items) − Sum of all N items.

Combined Average

If the average of n₁ items is A₁ and n₂ items is A₂, then their combined average is given by (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Weighted Average

It is an average resulting from the multiplication of each component by a factor reflecting its importance. Formula: (w₁x₁ + w₂x₂ + ... + wₙxₙ) ÷ (w₁ + w₂ + ... + wₙ).

questions.question: A man goes to Mumbai from Pune at a speed of 78km/hr and returns to Pune at speed of 91km/hr, through same route. What is his average speed (in km/hr) of the entire journey?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When a person covers two equal distances at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Given speeds are x = 78 km/hr and y = 91 km/hr.

Average Speed = (2 × 78 × 91) ÷ (78 + 91)

Average Speed = (2 × 78 × 91) ÷ 169

Average Speed = 2 × 6 × 7 = 84 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 84 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed from Pune to Mumbai = 78 km/hr

Speed from Mumbai to Pune = 91 km/hr

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 Pune
 Mumbai
 

 Speed = 78 km/hr
 

 Speed = 91 km/hr
 
• 
 Constant Distance (D)

**Formula Used:**

Average speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the one-way distance be the LCM of the speeds (78 and 91) to simplify calculations.

⇒ 78 = 13 × 6 and 91 = 13 × 7

⇒ LCM of 78 and 91 = 13 × 6 × 7 = 546

⇒ Let the distance between Pune and Mumbai be 546 km.

⇒ Time taken from Pune to Mumbai = Distance ÷ Speed = 546 ÷ 78 = 7 hours.

⇒ Time taken from Mumbai to Pune = Distance ÷ Speed = 546 ÷ 91 = 6 hours.

⇒ Total Distance covered = 546 + 546 = 1092 km.

⇒ Total Time taken = 7 + 6 = 13 hours.

⇒ Average Speed = 1092 ÷ 13 = 84 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 84 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Different Distances

When travelling different distances D₁, D₂ at speeds S₁, S₂ respectively, Average Speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time) = (D₁ + D₂) ÷ (D₁/S₁ + D₂/S₂).

Average Speed for 3 Equal Distances

When a person travels 3 equal distances at speeds x, y, and z, the Average Speed = 3xyz ÷ (xy + yz + zx).

Relative Speed

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). When moving in the same direction, it is the difference (S₁ − S₂).

questions.question: What is the effective discount per cent if a shopkeeper offers a scheme, “Buy five and get three free”?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective Discount % = (Free Items ÷ Total Items) × 100

Here, Free Items = 3

Total Items = 5 (Paid) + 3 (Free) = 8

Discount % = (3 ÷ 8) × 100 = 37.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 37.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 
 
 
 
 Buy 5 (Paid)
 
 
 
 
 
 Get 3 (Free)
 
 Total Items = 5 + 3 = 8
 

 Discount % = (3 ÷ 8) × 100 = 37.5%

**Given:**

Scheme = Buy 5, get 3 free.

**Formula Used:**

Discount % = (Total Discount ÷ Total Marked Price) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the marked price of 1 item be ₹10.

⇒ Total items taken by the customer = 5 (paid) + 3 (free) = 8 items.

⇒ Total marked price of 8 items = 8 × 10 = ₹80.

⇒ Total selling price (since customer pays for only 5 items) = 5 × 10 = ₹50.

⇒ Total Discount = Marked Price − Selling Price = 80 − 50 = ₹30.

⇒ Effective Discount % = (30 ÷ 80) × 100

⇒ Effective Discount % = (3 ÷ 8) × 100 = 37.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 37.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discount

When two discounts of a% and b% are given successively on an article, the net effective discount % is given by the formula: (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Marked Price and Cost Price Relation

The direct relationship between Cost Price (CP) and Marked Price (MP) when dealing with a profit P% and discount D% is: MP × (100 − D)% = CP × (100 + P)%.

Combined Free Scheme and Additional Discount

If a shopkeeper offers a "Buy X Get Y Free" scheme along with an additional z% discount, the overall Selling Price is given by: SP = MP × [X ÷ (X + Y)] × [(100 − z) ÷ 100].

questions.question: Manish travels from City A to City B. If Manish drives his car at 1/3​ of his normal speed, then he reaches City B 36 minutes late. Find the time (in minutes) that Manish would have taken to travel from City A to City B if he drove at his normal speed.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed ratio (Normal : New) = 3 : 1

Time ratio (Normal : New) = 1 : 3 (Since time is inversely proportional to speed)

Difference in time ratio = 3 − 1 = 2 units

2 units → 36 minutes late

1 unit (Normal time) → 18 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 18 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 
 
• 
 
 City A
 City B
 Distance = D
 
 
 Normal: Speed = S
 Time = T min
 
 
 New: Speed = S / 3
 Time = (T + 36) min

**Given:**

New speed = 1/3 of normal speed

Time delay = 36 minutes late

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

When distance is constant, Speed × Time = Constant

**Calculation:**

Let the normal speed be S and normal time be T.

⇒ Normal distance = S × T

⇒ New speed = S / 3

⇒ New time = T + 36

Since the distance traveled is the same in both cases:

⇒ S × T = (S / 3) × (T + 36)

⇒ T = (T + 36) / 3

⇒ 3T = T + 36

⇒ 2T = 36

⇒ T = 18 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 18 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportionality of Speed and Time

When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time. If speed is reduced to a/b of its original value, the time taken becomes b/a of the original time.

Average Speed

Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time. If two equal distances are covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy / (x + y).

Relative Speed

When two bodies move in the same direction, Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂|. When moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.
